label: prop:binding-error-amplification
title: Binding-energy error amplification: $\mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B$
html:
Write the binding energy as the mass defect

  B \;=\; M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{atom}},
  \qquad
  M_{\mathrm{free}} = \textstyle\sum_i \mathfrak{m}(\text{constituent}_i),

the difference between the free-constituent mass and the bound-state mass, with 0 < B \ll M_{\mathrm{atom}}. If the predicted bound-state mass carries relative error \delta,

  M_{\mathrm{atom}}^{\mathrm{pred}} = M_{\mathrm{atom}}\,(1+\delta),

and M_{\mathrm{free}} is taken exact, then the predicted binding B^{\mathrm{pred}} = M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{atom}}^{\mathrm{pred}} has relative error

  \frac{B^{\mathrm{pred}} - B}{B}
  \;=\; -\,\delta \cdot \frac{M_{\mathrm{atom}}}{B}.

The error is amplified by the dimensionless factor \mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
